title: Court booking lifecycle
idea: A court Booking is a state machine: PENDING until paid, then CONFIRMED, then COMPLETED or CANCELLED; an unpaid hold may expire or be cancelled.
points: A new Booking is PENDING and holds its hours until a deadline.
Payment moves PENDING to CONFIRMED; a missed deadline moves it to EXPIRED.
Only CANCELLED and EXPIRED give the court hours back.
CANCELLED, EXPIRED and COMPLETED are final: no move leaves them.

messages.label: hold(C-1, Fri 18:00, 2h)
messages.note: On Tuesday at 10:00 the player picks two Friday hours on the turf. The service creates BK-1 as PENDING with a ten-minute hold.

messages.label: reserveAll(18:00, 19:00)
messages.note: Both hours are reserved together, so no one else can take them.

messages.label: BK-1 PENDING, pay by 10:10
messages.note: The player gets a deadline to show as a countdown.

messages.label: pay(BK-1)
messages.note: Payment starts before the deadline. Page 3 did this inside one call; here it is a separate step.

messages.label: charge(160000)
messages.note: The service charges the price it froze at hold time.

messages.label: ok
messages.note: The charge succeeds, so BK-1 moves PENDING to CONFIRMED.

messages.label: cancel(BK-1)
messages.note: A day later, well before the game, the player cancels. CONFIRMED to CANCELLED is an allowed move.

messages.label: refundMinor(160000, start, now)
messages.note: CancellationPolicy, a new swappable rule like PricingStrategy, decides the refund from how early the player cancels.

messages.label: release(BK-1)
messages.note: CANCELLED frees the hours, so the grid shows them as free again.

messages.label: CANCELLED, refund issued
messages.note: If the deadline had passed before payment, BK-1 would be EXPIRED instead.

code.title: Status enum with rules
code.caption: The allowed moves live in the enum. Booking asks the enum before every change and reports when hours are freed.

walk.text: BK-1 is paid and played. A cancel after the game must be refused.
BK-2 expires unpaid, then a late payment tries to confirm it.
BK-3 is paid, then cancelled early.
An `EnumMap` lists the allowed next states. Final states map to an empty set.
One question for every move, and one rule for which states keep the hours.
An illegal move is reported and changes nothing.
A legal move updates status and says when the court hours go back.

pitfalls: Do not set status fields directly from controllers; always go through one transition method.
A late payment for an EXPIRED booking must be refunded, not confirmed.
Do not free hours on COMPLETED; past bookings stay in the history.

quiz.q: What does the third line of BookingStates print?
options: BK-1 COMPLETED -> CANCELLED (player cancels after the game)
BK-1 refused COMPLETED -> CANCELLED (player cancels after the game)
BK-1 CONFIRMED -> CANCELLED (player cancels after the game)
quiz.why: COMPLETED maps to an empty set of next states, so `canMoveTo` is false and `moveTo` prints the refusal without changing status.

takeaway: Allowed moves live in one table; anything else is refused.

starters: Should a no-show be its own state?
Who moves CONFIRMED bookings to COMPLETED, and when?
How do I handle a payment that succeeds after the hold expired?
